newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-DEWULF BEATS SICK ALONSO FOR SECOND TOUR WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DEWULF BEATS SICK ALONSO FOR SECOND TOUR WIN.

text.p: French Open semifinalist Filip Dewulf overcame ailing Spaniard Julian Alonso 7-6 6-4 6-1 at the Generali Open on Sunday for his second tournament victory.
Alonso, 19 and playing in only his third ATP event, chose to complete the clay-court final despite a slight temperature and a medical check-up at the start of the third set.
"I took his temperature but it was only a little bit above average," said ATP tour trainer Juergen Dess. "It was not high enough to order him to retire."
After the one-sided and bland match, Belgian Dewulf said he also was not 100 percent fit and had not played his best tennis.
"This was probably the worst match both of us played in this tournament. There were a lot of mistakes, we didn't find our rhythm and there were no rallies.
"But that happens sometimes," added number 10 seed Dewulf. "He had a lot of tough matches here and was very tired today. I think I was a bit fitter."
Dewulf, whose only other title was the 1995 CA-Trophy in Vienna when he defeated Thomas Muster on home soil, had a shaky start in the final here.
He dropped serve at 3-1 with a double fault, before stepping up a gear and breaking for 5-4. The set went into a tiebreak which the Belgian won 7-2.
Both players held serve in the second set until Dewulf broke a tired-looking Alonso in the last game for 6-4. He then had little trouble taking the final set with breaks at 3-1 and 6-1.
